title: restore transparent substrate recovery for MCP reads
description:
The canonical DuckDB substrate has been quarantined and rebuilt repeatedly after fatal ART/index failures. The current rebuilt database contains partial source tables but zero substrate_promotion_run/evidence_graph_build rows, while the status manifest belongs to an older 10.45 GB generation and is rejected by the current-file identity check.

Unpinned MCP read routes call ensure_substrate_materialized_for_read(), but evidence_graph_substrate has no entry in _materializers(). ensure_materialized() therefore returns blocked; callers discard that result and continue, yielding apparently successful empty data. Example: lynchpin_evidence(action=timeline, 2026-07-13..14) returned ok=true/data=[] even though readiness reports no promoted snapshot.

The intended contract is transparent materialization when a requested product/window is not materialized. Recovery must preserve that contract without hiding a failed convergence result.
acceptance_criteria:
1. After a clean-schema corruption rebuild, an unpinned MCP read transparently converges the required substrate/window when local sources permit.
2. If convergence cannot run or fails, the MCP response is explicitly blocked/error; it cannot return ok=true with a vacuous empty dataset.
3. Rebuild/recovery invalidates or regenerates the status manifest and read snapshot consistently with the canonical generation.
4. A behavior test reproduces valid promotion -> corrupt rebuild -> partial source refresh -> unpinned MCP read and proves recovery or explicit failure.

title: Recover and report GitHub substrate promotion failures
description: Chisel's GitHub-context refresh can hit a DuckDB fatal checkpoint error, after which materialize_github_context swallows the failure and Chisel prints a misleading ready status. Reproduce the connection-invalidated path, retry safely with a fresh connection where possible, and surface degraded promotion status without blocking NDJSON-backed snapshot generation.
acceptance_criteria: A transient DuckDB fatal during GitHub-context promotion gets one fresh-connection retry; persistent promotion failure is represented in the returned manifest and Chisel output does not claim an unqualified ready state; focused regression tests cover both cases.
notes: Root cause evidence: the canonical DuckDB failed standalone CHECKPOINT with TransformToDeprecated, and its read snapshot passed CHECKPOINT but aborted under promotion with GetAllocatorIdx. Snapshot reuse was unsafe. Implemented atomic clean-schema rebuild before quarantine/swap, one idempotent GitHub retry, fail-closed Chisel degradation, and multiline artifact-reference guarding found during full regeneration. Live recovery rebuilt 49 tables and populated core rows; forced 64-step current-state regeneration completed 63 steps plus a successful targeted rerun of the narrative; full five-repository Chisel regeneration completed with unqualified GitHub context ready and all XML well formed. Focused tests: 14 passed. Changed-file Ruff: passed. Publication checker required by instructions was absent from this checkout and PATH; complete public diff was manually reviewed. Residual Polylogue operator-day adapter drift tracked as lynchpin-4ul.
close_reason: Recovered via clean derived-store rebuild, regenerated all outputs, and verified post-Chisel checkpoint plus focused regressions.

title: ActivityWatch manifest covered_dates includes phantom 2010/2017-2018 dates with zero backing events
description:
events.manifest.json's covered_dates lists 3,456 dates from 2010-01-01 through 2026-07-13, but the real event data in events.ndjson only spans 2024-02-15 to 2026-07-12 (2,440,563 events, confirmed by direct earliest/latest inspection and a grep for 2017-01-30T returning zero matches). The bogus entries: 4 placeholder-looking dates (2010-01-01 through 2010-01-04, likely an uninitialized/default date artifact) and a full false 2017-01-30 through ~2018 span with no backing events.

Root cause: manifest_windows.py's merge_manifest_covered_dates() is purely accretive -- each materialization run unions the previously-recorded covered_dates with newly observed dates but never re-validates old entries against current event data (lynchpin/ingest/manifest_windows.py:35-56). Whatever produced the bad 2010/2017 dates once (early bug, stale fixture, bad merge) has been silently re-affirmed on every regeneration since, because nothing ever checks whether an old covered date still has real events.

Impact discovered 2026-08-02: this fed a wrong 'covers 9 years of ActivityWatch data' claim into the sleep_productivity join reporting (lynchpin/ingest/sleep_productivity_materialize.py consumes the same AW data) -- the real join window is ~2.4 years, not 9. Any other consumer trusting events.manifest.json's covered_dates/first_date/last_date for AW coverage claims is getting the same wrong answer.

Fix direction: either (a) make merge_manifest_covered_dates validate old entries still have backing events before carrying them forward (expensive, requires re-scanning), or (b) regenerate events.manifest.json from scratch (non-accretive) at least once to purge the phantom entries, then decide whether accretive merging is safe to keep going forward, or (c) add a sanity check/test asserting manifest first_date matches the true earliest event in events.ndjson.
close_reason: Root cause fixed in manifest_windows.py::merge_manifest_covered_dates() (verified_bounds parameter drops carried-forward dates outside the true min/max of the row set just materialized), wired into all 8 consumers, commit bac3190. events.manifest.json regenerated clean: 2010-01-01..2026-07-13/3456 dates -> 2024-02-15..2026-07-13/880 dates, verified against raw events.ndjson directly. Same audit found and fixed 4 more corrupted manifests (activitywatch/graph, IRC, atuin, spotify/daily) plus a blocking crash-on-malformed-line bug (commit b08b893). Follow-ups tracked separately: lynchpin-ee9 (unrelated keylog placeholder bug), lynchpin-mxo (atuin torn-line data loss), lynchpin-9vx (activitywatch_derived backlog), lynchpin-4pz (pytest ordering fragility). Report corrected at /realm/data/derived/reports/sleep-pipeline-audit-2026-08-02.html.

title: Honor repository LOC exclusions in Chisel
description: Chisel currently runs tokei with --no-ignore, bypassing repository .gitignore, .ignore, and .tokeignore policies and inflating attribution statistics with generated and internal agent surfaces. Restore native ignore semantics while keeping Chisel's explicit safety exclusions and hidden-file support.
design: Collect Tokei inputs from git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard so tracked source remains visible even when a broad local ignore matches it, while ignored runtime/demo corpora never enter the command. Keep explicit Chisel safety exclusions. Add a first-match Sinnix verification bucket. Derive default-branch Git growth series, bucket churn, commit-kind mix, rolling velocity, and a cross-project portfolio report with dependency-free SVG charts plus CSV/JSON/Markdown.
acceptance_criteria: Chisel excludes ignored local corpora and dependencies from LOC without hiding tracked repository surfaces; Sinnix checks are attributed to a dedicated tests bucket; growth outputs include per-project daily/weekly/monthly data, summary and bucket analysis, plus a cross-project Markdown/JSON/CSV/SVG portfolio; tests prove ignore-aware input selection, test bucketing, history aggregation, and report generation; focused Chisel tests and Ruff pass.
close_reason: Chisel now honors repository LOC policy, attributes Sinnix checks separately, emits rename-aware growth and Beads history analyses, and packages a complete browsable Beads board. Ruff, 34 focused tests, and real four-project generation passed.

title: pytest -q (full suite) has order-dependent failures unrelated to any specific change
description:
Discovered while verifying the lynchpin-jzb fix: running the whole suite
(direnv exec . pytest -q, no -k) produced 407 failed / 4 errored tests
spanning wholly unrelated subsystems (tests/test_materialization.py,
tests/substrate/test_substrate_views.py, tests/substrate/test_work_observations.py,
tests/substrate/test_prune_commit_history.py). Every failing test passes
when its file is run in isolation (verified for test_materialization.py:
111 passed standalone vs many failures in the full run) and the specific
files touched by lynchpin-jzb (tests/ingest/*) pass both standalone and in
the full run. This points to shared global state leaking across test
modules when the whole suite runs together (module-level caches, monkeypatch
scope, or a shared DuckDB/config singleton not reset between files) rather
than to any single change. Not investigated further or fixed here -- out of
scope for the manifest-corruption bug. Filing so this known fragility is
tracked instead of silently re-discovered by the next agent that runs the
full suite and assumes their change broke 400 tests.

title: activitywatch_derived has a ~1.7yr materialization backlog (2024-02-15..2026-03-15 never computed)
description:
Found auditing manifests for lynchpin-jzb. events.manifest.json (raw AW
events) now correctly covers 2024-02-15..2026-07-12 after the lynchpin-jzb
fix, but /realm/data/derived/lynchpin/activitywatch/graph/manifest.json
(activitywatch_derived: focus_spans, daily_activity, deep_work, circadian,
loops, fragmentation, attention, project_focus_days) only has real coverage
from 2026-03-16 onward -- a genuine backlog, not corruption (verified: no
gaps within the covered span, and the pre-2026-03-16 claim was just 3
phantom placeholder dates already purged by the lynchpin-jzb fix).

This is a legitimate materialization-completeness gap: ~761 real days of AW
events (2024-02-15..2026-03-15) have never been through
activitywatch_derived, so anything reading daily_activity/focus_spans/etc
for that period (e.g. lifestyle-correlation or productivity analyses) is
silently missing ~1.7 years of derived signal even though the raw events
exist. Not fixed here: a full backfill run over that span is a
non-trivial compute job (the equivalent narrow-window run for a single day
took several minutes; a ~760-day backfill was judged out of scope for a
manifest-corruption bugfix pass and risked a multi-hour unattended run).

title: personal_daily_signals has spurious zero-value keylog rows for 2010-2012 (pre-capture dates)
description:
Discovered while auditing manifest_windows.py consumers for the lynchpin-jzb
class of corruption (manifest covered_dates claiming coverage wider than real
data). /realm/data/derived/lynchpin/personal/daily_signals.ndjson contains
4372 keylog rows dated 2010-01-04 through ~2012, all with value=0.0 -- a
structural placeholder pattern (keylog.daily_activity() builds a dense
per-day dict defaulting every metric to 0 for every day in [start,end),
regardless of whether keylog ever captured that day). scribe-tap/keylog
capture did not exist in 2010-2012, so these are not real "zero activity"
observations.

Root cause is different from lynchpin-jzb: this is not manifest_windows.py's
accretive merge (personal_daily_signals's own manifest is internally
consistent with its row data, so the shared verified_bounds fix does not
touch it). The likely cause is materialize_personal_daily_signals()'s
default (start=None) path, which derives its full backfill window from
`min(first_date)`..`max(last_date)` across ALL "ready" audited sources
(_personal_daily_signal_rows_with_inputs() in
lynchpin/ingest/personal_signals_materialize.py:214-229) -- if any single
source's audited first_date is wrong (e.g. the AW manifest bug that this
window's sibling fix just corrected, or another source's own bad bound),
every adapter with a naive dense per-day fill (like keylog) will backfill
placeholder rows across the entire union window, not just its own real
coverage. Also worth checking whether keylog's own `_overlaps()` gate
(materialized_dataset_overlaps) should have excluded 2010-2012 and didn't.

Also note: google_takeout genuinely has 219 real nonzero rows in the same
2010-2012 span (real historical Google account activity), so a blind
date-range purge of that window is NOT safe -- only the keylog rows are
spurious. Any fix needs to be source-specific.

Not fixed in this pass (out of scope for lynchpin-jzb): fixing correctly
requires tracing keylog's real capture start date and auditing
`_window_personal_daily_signal_rows`'s per-source overlap gating, which is
a separate investigation.

title: atuin history.ndjson had a torn/corrupt line (data loss, one command lost)
description:
Found while regenerating the atuin manifest for lynchpin-jzb: line 12510 of
/realm/data/captures/shell/atuin/history.ndjson was a truncated JSON
fragment (`wd": "/home/sinity/realm/dev/proj/intercept-bounce", "duration_ns":
8204933943, ...}` -- missing its `{"command": "...", "c` prefix), which
crashed materialize_atuin_history() with json.decoder.JSONDecodeError
whenever it tried to read existing rows for an incremental merge. This
looks like a torn write (two writes interleaved without a clean newline
boundary), not disk corruption -- adjacent lines 12508/12509/12511/12512
are intact and chronologically sensible.

Immediate fix (landed as part of the lynchpin-jzb PR, not a dedicated
follow-up): hardened _read_existing_rows() in terminal_materialize.py (and
the equivalent readers in irc_materialize.py, temporal_signals_materialize.py,
sleep_productivity_materialize.py, activitywatch_derived_materialize.py,
personal_signals_materialize.py x2, webhistory.py) to skip malformed JSON
lines instead of crashing the whole materializer run, matching the pattern
already used in activitywatch_materialize.py.

Not fixed: the one truncated command entry itself is unrecoverable (its
prefix is gone) and was silently dropped on the next materialize run. This
bead tracks two follow-ups: (1) whether the write path that produces
history.ndjson (or a concurrent writer) can tear lines and needs a
write-then-rename or lock discipline fix, and (2) whether it's worth a
one-time audit of other high-volume append-only ndjson sources for the same
torn-line pattern now that several readers were silently crash-prone to it.
